He thinks there is **a coin — a piece of money lying on the floor — under his shoe**. ## The film and the people in the shot

The video is Charlie Chaplin's two-reel comedy **_The Immigrant_ (1917)**, and the passage in question is the restaurant sequence in the second half of the picture (from roughly 18:30 onwards in this copy).

3. **About 18:56–18:58.** Back in the wide shot, he hands the customer on the left his change, turns, and walks off to the back of the room. The coin is left lying on the floor.

Then at about **19:45**, as Chaplin's hand actually closes on the coin at his shoe, he **jerks his right foot up off the floor with the knee bent, shakes and waggles it, peers down at it, and then straightens up and searches the floor all round his feet with his eyes** — the exact pantomime of a man who is convinced he has something underfoot and wants to see what it is. 8. **He finds nothing**, because the Tramp has just got the coin away. He gives it up and goes straight over to the Tramp's table with the bill.
